key_insight: Empirical squared residuals can be converted into pointwise error bounds for mesh-free solvers of Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equations on unbounded domains, enabling convergence guarantees for both kernel collocation and PINNs.
engineering_relevance: This gives practical a posteriori error control for large-scale optimal control and PDE solvers when meshing is difficult or impossible, especially on unbounded domains.
method: Wendland-kernel collocation with a native-space norm constraint; convergence depends on fill distance.
Physics-informed neural networks with smooth activations and a Sobolev-norm constraint; convergence is in probability with high-probability bounds.
Use empirical-to-population estimates plus an interpolation inequality to turn $L^2$ residuals into sup-norm control, with domain-truncation error quantified.
evidence_signal: The paper provides theoretical convergence and quantitative error bounds, and validates them with numerical experiments in one and two spatial dimensions.
watch_item: The guarantees require additional regularity assumptions beyond viscosity well-posedness, and the neural-network result is probabilistic rather than deterministic.
paper_title: Convergence of kernel and neural-network methods for Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations on unbounded domains
